title: Arteries vs veins: thick walls or valves?
examples: What is the difference between arteries and veins?
Why do arteries have thick walls?

explain.say: Press two fingers gently on the inside of your wrist. Can you feel a beat? That is an artery. Now look at the blue-ish lines on the back of your hand. Those are veins. Let's compare these two kinds of blood tube.

explain.say: Look at the left side: arteries. They carry blood away from the heart, at high pressure, in spurts. So they have thick, stretchy, muscly walls that do not burst. Here is a trick: A for artery, A for away. Which way do arteries carry blood?

explain.say: Now the right side: veins. They bring blood back to the heart, slowly, at low pressure. Their walls are thin and the space inside is wide. Why might they not need thick walls?

explain.say: See the last line on the veins side? Because the pressure is low, veins have valves, little flaps that only open one way, so blood cannot slip backwards, even up your legs. What might happen without them?

faq.q: Why do arteries have thick walls?
faq.a: Blood leaves the heart at high pressure. Thick walls with muscle and elastic tissue stop arteries bursting and stretch and spring back with each beat, smoothing the flow.
Veins carry blood back to the heart at low pressure. They have thin walls, a wide space inside called the lumen, and valves.
Blood in veins moves slowly at low pressure. Valves are one-way flaps that stop blood flowing backwards, especially in the legs, where it must travel up against gravity.
asks: What do valves in veins do?

faq.a: Capillaries are tiny blood vessels with walls only one cell thick. They link arteries to veins, and substances like oxygen, glucose and carbon dioxide pass through their walls.
asks: How do arteries connect to veins?

faq.a: A pulse is the stretch of an artery each time the heart pushes blood into it. You can feel it in your wrist or neck and count it to find your heart rate.
asks: How do I find my pulse?

facts: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood back to it.
Capillary walls are only one cell thick.
The blood vessels of an adult are often estimated at about 100,000 km long in total.

quiz.why: Veins have valves to stop low-pressure blood flowing backwards.

wrong.0: High pressure keeps blood moving forward in arteries, so they do not need valves.
wrong.2: Capillaries are tiny and have no valves.

quiz.say: Why can you feel a pulse in an artery but not in a vein?
